one_liner: Datadog has a broad REST API with self-serve API/app keys and PATs; OAuth exists but is limited to approved partners; an official remote MCP server exists; builder access is via a 14-day free trial.
auth_notes: Users generate an API key + application key (headers DD-API-KEY / DD-APPLICATION-KEY), or newer Personal Access Tokens. Datadog does document an OAuth2 authorization-code + PKCE flow, but OAuth clients are created in a Datadog Partner Sandbox Account / Developer Platform for Marketplace integrations, and the earlier-fetched integration docs say standalone OAuth clients are not supported. So OAUTH2 is not counted as available to a general third-party developer. Composio's catalog lists OAUTH2 (probably via partner registration), which is the flagged discrepancy; the pages do not show self-serve OAuth app registration.
access_notes: Datadog's blog says new users can sign up for a free 14-day trial. The pages do not mention a permanent free tier. Keys are created inside a Datadog org.
blocker_notes: Builder access is via a short 14-day trial. Multi-user OAuth is limited to partner-registered clients, so the toolkit must use per-customer API/app keys or PATs.

evidence.quote: Authenticate to the API with an [API key](https://docs.datadoghq.com/account_management/api-app-keys/#api-keys) using the header `DD-API-KEY`.
Unlike application keys, PATs do not need to be paired with an API key.
OAuth is available only to approved Technology Partners developing official Datadog integrations. Standalone OAuth clients are not supported.
Within your Datadog Partner Sandbox Account, create and configure your OAuth client in the [Developer Platform](https://app.datadoghq.com/publishing-platform).
